description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 after a scoping pass at dd07432db. TWO OF THE THREE
READER GAPS ARE CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT OR BY DELETION; what remains is the site
numbering and a set of stale documents.

GAP (1) -- blind_escapes bailing on early.len() != late.len() -- IS PRESENT
AND REACHED but SKIPS NOTHING. Instrumented walk at settled: 87 pairs over 79
readable plans, 36 Separated, 51 Covering, 0 Escaping, and ZERO length-guard
skips. The guard is inert because the PLAN-level skip already removes every
plan whose arms could ask different subject sets. (It would skip 5 under the
extended reader fz-kdt.187 proposed, and that extension is now withdrawn.)
GAP (2) -- separated_somewhere consulting only `early`s subjects -- IS MOOT:
that function was introduced by fz-kdt.178 (8de517a28) and DELETED by
fz-kdt.186 (accb5cfbe), replaced by `seating`. `seating` has the same
asymmetry but enforces equal lengths, and 0 mismatches were measured, so no
late-only subject can be missed.

GAP (3) -- dump wN != census wN -- IS STILL TRUE and is now the whole ticket.
The canon dump prints `wrapper w{canonical}` from ProgramCanon::wrapper_order
(a sort over a rendered key) while PlanSite::Selection prints
`wrapper.identity` (the published index). Measured, with canon.rs instrumented
to print both: 00277 maps w0->w4, w1->w2, w2->w3, w3->w0, w4->w1 with NO fixed
points; enum_map_family w0->w11, w1->w0, ... w11->w10; enum_take_drop_split and
00420 w0->w25, w1->w26, w2->w36, ... w35->w0. So a reader following a wrapper
number from a doc or a failure message into a dump lands on the wrong wrapper.

NOTHING NAMES A CENSUS WRAPPER NUMBER ANY MORE, so this is a latent trap
rather than a live wrong answer: INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_POPULATION is `&[]`
(fz-kdt.199), SOURCE_ORDER_BLIND_ESCAPES is `&[]` and source-order only (never
a Selection site), and SOURCE_ORDER_PLANS_ON_THE_CENSUS is keyed by kind. The
`executable N` / `e<N>` positional-index half of the original ticket is
constant-free now too. What survives is (a) the gates` FAILURE MESSAGES, which
would print w{identity} on a future red, and (b) STALE PROSE that reads as
fact and is not.

THE CHANGE: PlanSite::Selection`s Display renders the CANONICAL number the
dump prints -- reuse canon`s wrapper_order, or render
`wrapper w{canonical} (published w{identity})`. Gate: a unit test that drives
enum_map_family, takes the PlanSite::Selection label for a known plan and
asserts it names the same wrapper canon_backend_program heads that block with.
RED AT HEAD (identity 11 versus canonical 0), green after.

IN THE SAME COMMIT, fix the documents that are stale at head -- this is a
house-law matter, they are written as provable present-tense fact and are not:
dispatch-matrix.md:808 (names w13-w19), callsite_dispatch.rs:2599 (w13),
drive_test.rs:9034 (w15/w18/w19) and drive_test.rs:9945 (w21-w24). NOTE 00277
HAS FIVE WRAPPERS AT HEAD, so w13-w20 exist in NEITHER numbering. And refresh
dispatch-matrix.md`s census table, which says call-edge 17 / entry 153,146 /
selection 86 / Region::List 87 / 44 groups; measured now: 21 / 169,162 / 49 /
103 / 0.

LAND LAST of the three instrument tickets: fz-kdt.187 touches
SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS`s doc and fz-kdt.196 touches the census gate`s doc,
so this ticket corrects both in one pass.

comments.text: fz-kdt.179 landed (c3e27143d): member selection now runs the seat, but your two reader gaps are UNCHANGED and one is now the last census standing. INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_POPULATION (kept at 44 groups) still names CENSUS wrapper numbers, which differ from dump wN -- your dump-wN-vs-census-wN gap. And the static census reader's arm-pair skipping is retired for the SEAT census here but your description covers the reading logic that INDISTINGUISHABLE still uses. Re-measure against this base: the seat census is gone, so your scope narrows to INDISTINGUISHABLE's numbering and any reader the entry/case/receive censuses still use.

title: The static census reader skips arm pairs that ask different subject sets and consults separating subjects only on the earlier arm, where production covers walks the full position vector; and dump wrapper numbers differ from census wrapper numbers
